With 5,400+ employees and over 80,000 institutional, commercial, and payments clients, we operate from more than 80 offices spread across six continents. Corporate: Engage in a deep variety of business-critical activities that keep our company running efficiently. From strategic marketing and financial management to human resources and operational oversight, you’ll have the opportunity to optimize processes and implement game-changing policies.

Position Purpose

We are seeking a seasoned professional to join as Senior Specialist, PR & Communications. This individual will collaborate with Commercial & Payments business leaders, executives, subject matter experts, spokespeople and marketing teams to deliver clear, consistent and compelling messaging and stories with the media and across key communications channels.

The role will create, drive and implement communications strategies supporting StoneX's Commercial & Payments businesses, develop strong relationships across a diverse and specialized business, manage relationships with tier 1 media, financial, trade and commodity media, and drive performance against strategic goals — including brand awareness, executive and subject-matter-expert visibility through media coverage, thought leadership, events and presentations, employee advocacy and additional marketing initiatives.

Working closely with Commercial & Payments marketing leads, business development and business stakeholders, the role will connect communications activity to commercial priorities, market positioning, client themes and growth initiatives across the Commercial & Payments platform.

Global alignment is a core expectation of the role. The Commercial & Payments PR & Communications Manager will work closely with the UK and APAC PR & Communications Managers and the Global Brand team to ensure Commercial & Payments messaging, media strategy, executive positioning and thought leadership are coordinated across regions and consistently reinforce StoneX's global Commercial & Payments narrative.

Responsibilities

Primary duties will include

• Manage and execute strategic communications for StoneX's Commercial & Payments businesses, aligned with communications, marketing and business objectives.
• Develop strong working relationships with Commercial & Payments business leaders, sales and risk management teams, commodity and FX specialists, payments product teams and other subject-matter experts to identify timely and differentiated communications opportunities.
• Develop and manage relationships between tier 1 media, financial, trade and commodity media and StoneX representatives.
• Proactively pitch StoneX businesses, executives, brokers/traders, analysts and market experts for commentary, thought leadership and other relevant opportunities for exposure.
• Identify opportunities to elevate StoneX's commodity, foreign exchange, risk management and payments expertise around relevant market developments, trends, products and client themes.
• Draft press materials, talking points, executive op-eds, thought-leadership content and marketing communications.
• Train and support StoneX representatives for various media formats, including interviews, panels, broadcast appearances and other external engagements.
• Partner with Marketing and business stakeholders to connect media relations and thought leadership with broader Commercial & Payments initiatives, including events, digital content, campaigns and client-facing programs.
• Support communications surrounding significant business developments, including new capabilities, product launches, strategic hires, geographic expansion, partnerships and other Commercial & Payments growth initiatives.
• Provide crisis and issues management support to Commercial & Payments and global leadership.
• Oversee media monitoring to track relevant market and business coverage and guide strategy based on positive and negative media trends.
• Develop strong relationships across the Commercial & Payments ecosystem, with Commercial & Payments Business Development as the primary strategic partner and Central Marketing as the second core partner, followed by Product, Legal, Compliance, HR, Online Reputation Management, Executive teams and other relevant stakeholders.
• Work in tandem with Commercial & Payments Business Development to maintain connectivity across Commercial & Payments stakeholders, ensuring communications strategies and external positioning reflect the broader commercial strategy, business priorities and cross-platform opportunities being advanced across the Commercial & Payments organization.
• Partner closely with Commercial & Payments Business Development and business stakeholders to understand commercial priorities, market positioning, client themes and growth initiatives, translating those priorities into relevant communications strategies and opportunities.
• Coordinate closely with the UK and APAC PR & Communications Managers to align Commercial & Payments messaging, share market intelligence and media opportunities, coordinate cross-regional executive and SME visibility, and ensure locally relevant communications remain consistent with StoneX's global Commercial & Payments positioning.
• Coordinate with other regional communications colleagues to identify opportunities to extend Commercial & Payments stories and subject-matter expertise across markets while maintaining alignment with global communications priorities.
• Develop frameworks for Commercial & Payments communications strategies, including performance metrics, in alignment with communications leadership expectations and global frameworks.
• Provide timely impact reports on Commercial & Payments communications strategies and activity.
• Own measurable outcomes for Commercial & Payments communications performance, including media coverage volume and quality, share of voice vs. competitors, and executive/SME visibility, reporting results against defined KPIs and taking corrective action when targets are missed.
• Be accountable for the accuracy, compliance and risk profile of all external-facing communications and media engagements for the segment, ensuring materials are vetted with Legal/Compliance and that reputational or regulatory risks are flagged and managed proactively.
• Own end-to-end press release execution for the segment, including timing and scheduling, platform posting, distribution, performance metrics and amplification across owned and earned channels.
• Other related communications duties as needed.

Qualifications

To land this role you will need:

• 8–10+ years of experience in corporate communications, public relations or media relations, preferably with a mix of in-house and agency roles.
• Exceptional written and verbal communications skills.
• Experience and comfort working with and influencing senior leaders and highly specialized subject-matter experts.
• Keen attention to detail.
• Strong relationships with top-tier financial, business, trade and commodity media in the United States, particularly across agriculture, energy and payments
• Ability to distill complex financial products, market developments and Commercial & Payments business concepts into clear narratives across varied audiences and formats.
• Experience with metrics-based and sentiment-based communications reporting.
• Experience integrating media outreach with broader marketing initiatives, such as thought leadership, events, campaigns and digital content.
• Ability to develop and coordinate communications across multiple Commercial & Payments businesses and subject-matter areas, connecting distinct business priorities and areas of expertise into a coherent StoneX Commercial & Payments narrative.
• Demonstrated ability to coordinate communications across regions, partnering with UK and APAC counterparts to balance local market relevance with consistent global Commercial & Payments messaging.

What makes you stand out:

• Experience within commodities, foreign exchange, payments or a similarly complex and highly regulated industry strongly preferred.

Education / Certification Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, English or a similar field of study.

Working Style:

• 4 days per week onsite, 1 day per week remote
• Ability to work independently and across global teams.
• Experience working in matrixed, international organizations and cross-functional teams.
• Flexibility to operate across time zones to support business and high-priority communications.

jobs.description: Summary: This role builds and supports the automations and AI-enabled workflows that cut manual effort, strengthen controls, and modernize recurring routines across technology cost, Cloud FinOps, TCO, productivity, portfolio, demand, procurement, headcount, and operational reporting. The work is to replace manual follow-up, spreadsheet checks, and point solutions with governed automation that has clear ownership, reliable support, and measurable value. Who We Are Looking For The Technology Financial Operations Office is looking for a hands-on AI & Automation Engineer to be based in Dublin. The broader team is distributed, with several senior stakeholders and complementary roles based in other offices, so this role will need to partner effectively across locations. The role analyzes how work gets done today, builds the workflow automation and AI tooling to do it better, and supports it once it is live. This role requires comfort with both business users and technical partners, and the ability to turn a manual routine into automation. The role uses approved enterprise platforms and responsible AI patterns, and is judged on what reaches production and gets used. Why This Role Is Important To Us The Technology Financial Operations Office is moving recurring work off manually maintained spreadsheets, inbox-driven follow-up, and one-off outputs. This role does the building: solving each problem with emerging technology, applying common standards, and reusing the result across functions instead of rebuilding it for every process. Near-term opportunities include intake and triage automation, procurement and TPRM knowledge assistance, PO/GL and accrual checks, timesheet and headcount agents, productivity initiative tracking, and support for IT TCO and FinOps tooling. Success looks like automations running in production, used by the teams they were built for, clearly owned and supported, and cutting manual effort without weakening controls. What You Will Be Responsible For Identify and prioritize automation opportunities across Technology Financial Operations Office functions based on value, repeatability, risk, control needs, and maintainability. Partner with business SMEs to map current processes, simplify where appropriate, and translate requirements into workflow designs, control points, exception paths, and support needs. Build, deploy, and support automations using approved enterprise tools, including Microsoft Power Platform, workflow technologies, AI-enabled productivity tools, and related integration patterns. Use AI where cost returns value: intake triage, knowledge assistance, document and data review, exception identification, summarization, routing, and human-in-the-loop decision support. Support TCO, FinOps, productivity, portfolio, demand, procurement, headcount, and operational reporting routines by automating intake, validation, exception management, workflow routing, and recurring checks. Run automations as supported products, with documentation, monitoring, release discipline, user guidance, a clear route for reporting issues, and a plan for improving them over time. Work with data, BI, app ownership, architecture, security, risk, controls, audit, and responsible AI partners to ensure solutions are compliant, auditable, secure, and supportable. Track outcomes such as effort avoided, cycle-time reduction, error reduction, control improvement, adoption, and user satisfaction. The instinct to ask whether a process should be simplified or retired before it gets automated. A realistic view of what AI does well, what it does badly, and where it can and cannot run autonomously. Treating controls, testing, and auditability as part of the design rather than a step at the end. Clear communication style for non-technical SMEs, finance partners, technology teams, and senior stakeholders. Willingness to own what is built after launch, including releases, documentation, controls, and results. Required Qualifications Experience designing, building, and supporting workflow automations, low-code solutions, AI-enabled assistants, or similar enterprise productivity tools. Hands-on experience with Microsoft Power Platform, Power Automate, Copilot & Copilot Studio, and AI-enabled productivity tools, SharePoint, Power BI, or comparable enterprise automation technologies. Experience mapping business processes, documenting requirements, designing future-state workflows, and supporting adoption with non-technical stakeholders. Understanding data handling, access control, auditability, testing, change management, and support expectations in a governed enterprise environment. Strong analytical and prioritization skills, with a track record of choosing which opportunities to pursue and which to decline. Preferred Qualifications Experience with enterprise AI or agentic workflow patterns, including retrieval-based assistants, knowledge bases, routing agents, review assistants, or workflow copilots. Experience with financial services, technology business management, FinOps, IT TCO, procurement, third-party risk, portfolio management, or technology finance operations. Experience operating under SDLC, end-user developed tool, model risk, data governance, responsible AI, or similar control frameworks. • Proactively reach out to and collaborate with diverse internal and external stakeholders to deeply understand their business models, needs, and operational goals.

• Lead regulatory strategy and manage interactions, inquiries, and investigations with key government authorities (e.g., Customs).

• Native or bilingual proficiency in both English and Korean, with exceptional ability to communicate with executive leadership in both languages.
• Exceptional commercial contract drafting and negotiation skills.
• Highly proactive attitude with a demonstrated willingness to learn new business areas and initiate cross-functional collaboration.
• Extensive experience in commercial transactions, regulatory compliance, corporate governance, and consumer protection laws.

Preferred Qualifications

• Knowledge of cross-border e-commerce operations, international trade, and global supply chain dynamics.
• Familiarity with relevant cross-border regulations, specifically Customs Law and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
• Proven track record of successfully managing regulatory audits, investigations, and direct communications with Korean regulatory bodies (e.g., Customs).
• Exceptional business acumen with the ability to think strategically, make practical decisions in ambiguous situations, and balance legal risk against business objectives.
• Demonstrated ability to influence, align, and lead cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders without formal authority.

About the team

The Applied AI Engineering team works closely with frontier startups. We are trusted advisors to, and thought partners with, startups to ensure that OpenAI’s technology is deployed safely and effectively, whilst also partnering with engineering, research, and product to turn those insights into evaluation systems, product improvements, and better model behavior.

This team sits at the intersection of customer reality and model quality. We combine hands-on technical depth with strong product judgment, helping translate complex, high-value use cases into clear signals that can improve both the customer experience and the underlying systems.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex for startups, you will help developers and founders transform how they build and ship software. You’ll combine hands-on engineering, startup experience, and compelling technical communication to help teams turn the potential of AI coding tools into practical, effective workflows.

Presentations and community engagement are central to this role. You will engage developers and founders through technical talks, live demos, workshops, and programmes across the startup ecosystem, alongside targeted work with individual customers. You’ll build reusable tools and resources that extend your impact, and bring insights from developers back to OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

This role is well suited to someone who enjoys both hands-on building and sharing what they learn with others. You should be as excited to lead a room of developers, deliver an engaging presentation, and build relationships across the startup community as you are to explore a technical problem in code—with a focus on sustained adoption and meaningful improvements in how startups work.

In this role, you will:

- Partner with top startups to identify where Codex can have the greatest impact on how their teams build and ship software.

- Design and lead technical talks, live demos, workshops, hackathons, and repeatable hands-on programmes that turn initial interest into sustained adoption.

- Work directly with selected customers to build Codex workflows, integrations, and automations, resolve technical blockers, and evaluate effectiveness and reliability.

- Turn successful approaches into reusable code examples, guides, and tools that help more startups succeed with Codex and OpenAI’s broader platform.

- Collaborate with account teams, developer experience, and ecosystem partners to reach developers and founders, prioritise opportunities, and drive measurable customer value.

- Translate customer experiences and developer feedback into actionable insights for OpenAI’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

- Have experience building at, founding, or working closely with early-stage startups, and understand the pace, ambiguity, and practical trade-offs involved.

- Bring strong software engineering fundamentals and enjoy building practical AI applications, integrations, and developer tools.

- Are an active user of Codex or other AI coding tools, with a thoughtful perspective on how they can improve software development.

- Are a compelling communicator who enjoys presenting, delivering live demos, and leading hands-on workshops for developers and founders.

- Have a talent for turning complex technical ideas into clear explanations, engaging examples, and reusable resources that help others succeed.

- Combine developer empathy with sound technical judgment: you can uncover what a team needs, troubleshoot problems, and help them adopt effective, reliable workflows.

- Bring high agency, curiosity, and end-to-end ownership, working independently while collaborating closely with colleagues and ecosystem partners.
